vectors.name: session
vectors.why: An owner signs a key their page reads with, at one host, for 12 hours at most.

vectors.name: session_by_a_file_key
vectors.why: An owner whose key is a file signs one the same way.

vectors.name: session_signed_in_one_touch_with_something_else
vectors.why: A session can be one of the objects one touch signs.

vectors.name: session_over
vectors.why: A session ends.

vectors.name: session_dated_ahead
vectors.why: It can't start later than the owner's clock allows.

vectors.name: session_for_more_than_12_hours
vectors.why: A session lasts 12 hours at most.

vectors.name: session_for_another_host
vectors.why: A session reads at the host it names, so one host can't use it at another.

vectors.name: session_naming_another_owner
vectors.why: It names the owner whose key signed it.

vectors.name: session_signed_by_another_owner
vectors.why: Another owner's session, read as this owner's, is checked under this owner's key, so it reads nothing of theirs.

vectors.name: session_signed_by_another_key
vectors.why: Another key signing in this owner's name verifies nothing.

vectors.name: session_by_a_stand_in
vectors.why: A stand-in's key is on an agent's machine, so it starts no session.

vectors.name: session_by_a_guest
vectors.why: Only a link reads a guest's ID, so it starts no session.

vectors.name: session_in_another_field_order
vectors.why: One encoding.

vectors.name: session_with_a_key_that_isnt_a_point
vectors.why: The key is a P-256 point.

vectors.name: session_over_4_kib
vectors.why: A session is read on every call before its signature is checked, so it's 4 KiB at most.

vectors.name: read_by_a_session
vectors.why: The session key signs one call, naming its session, as an agent's access proof does.

vectors.name: read_at_another_host
vectors.why: A proof for one host can't be used at another.

vectors.name: read_by_another_method
vectors.why: Or with another method.

vectors.name: read_of_another_path
vectors.why: Or on another path.

vectors.name: read_with_another_body
vectors.why: Or with another body.

vectors.name: read_under_another_session
vectors.why: A proof names the one session it's under.

vectors.name: read_proven_by_another_key
vectors.why: Only the session's key signs for it.

vectors.name: read_proven_under_the_type_agents_use
vectors.why: A session's proof has its own type, so nothing signed as an agent's access proof stands for one.

vectors.name: read_proven_too_late
vectors.why: A proof lasts the clock tolerance.

vectors.name: read_after_the_session_ended
vectors.why: A proof can't outlast its session.

vectors.name: approval_signed_by_a_session_key
vectors.why: A session never stands in for the owner's key, so a yes it signs is no yes.

vectors.name: agents_list
vectors.why: The owner's list of their agents, sealed to their own sealing key and again to their backup, kept at their page's host under their passkey's user handle.

vectors.name: agents_list_for_another_host
vectors.why: A list is kept at the host it names.

vectors.name: agents_list_naming_another_owner
vectors.why: It names the owner whose key signed it.

vectors.name: agents_list_signed_by_a_session_key
vectors.why: A list is the owner's signature, never a session's.

vectors.name: agents_list_dated_ahead
vectors.why: It can't be dated later than the owner's clock allows.

vectors.name: agents_list_too_short_to_be_sealed
vectors.why: What's in it is sealed, so it's at least a sealed note's key and tag.

vectors.name: agents_list_with_padding
vectors.why: A sealed note has one spelling.

vectors.name: agents_list_with_no_recovery_copy
vectors.why: The copy sealed to the owner's backup is a sealed note too.

vectors.name: agents_list_with_a_handle_in_capitals
vectors.why: A handle is 32 bytes in lowercase hex, so one owner's has one spelling.

vectors.name: agents_list_by_a_stand_in
vectors.why: A stand-in's key is on an agent's machine, so it keeps no owner's list.

vectors.name: agents_list_by_a_guest
vectors.why: Nor does a guest's, which only a link reads.

vectors.name: agents_list_with_a_short_handle
vectors.why: A page makes a 32-byte handle.

vectors.name: agents_list_opened
vectors.why: The owner's page opens the list with the sealing key their ID names, under associated data naming them, and shows each agent as they listed it. `sealing` is that key's private scalar in hex.

vectors.name: agents_list_saying_the_code_was_saved
vectors.why: It can say the owner saved their recovery code, or doesn't want to be told again, so no device of theirs asks.

vectors.name: agents_list_saying_the_code_isnt_saved_yet
vectors.why: The page always writes it, 0 until then, so the sealed size doesn't tell a host who skipped their code.

vectors.name: agents_list_from_a_computer
vectors.why: A computer's sign-in says of every agent whether its Signet runs on that computer, 1 or 0, so a recovery after losing it brings those back there, and the sealed size doesn't say how many.

vectors.name: agents_list_saying_beside_the_owner_as_2
vectors.why: Only 1 or 0.

vectors.name: agents_list_saying_beside_the_owner_as_true
vectors.why: It's one digit, so it's one width either way.

vectors.name: agents_list_saying_beside_the_owner_as_null
vectors.why: It's left out or a digit, so a reader can't take a null as either.

vectors.name: owner_list_handle
vectors.why: A computer's sign-in names its list by the SHA-256 of `splint owner list handle v1` and the owner's backup's point, which only the recovery code gives, so the code alone finds it.

vectors.name: owner_list_handle_of_no_point
vectors.why: A handle is made from the backup's point alone, so anything else names none.

vectors.name: agents_list_naming_another_owners_backup
vectors.why: What's sealed names the owner's own backup key, which their ID commits to, so a list made for someone else isn't taken.

vectors.name: agents_list_with_an_agent_twice
vectors.why: No agent's ID twice.

vectors.name: agents_list_saying_the_code_was_saved_as_true
vectors.why: It's one digit, 1 or 0, so it's one width either way.

vectors.name: agents_list_saying_the_code_was_saved_as_2
vectors.why: Only 1 or 0.

vectors.name: agents_list_with_a_hidden_character_in_a_label
vectors.why: A label is shown to the owner as their own words, so it has no hidden characters.

vectors.name: agents_list_sealed_for_another_owner
vectors.why: Sealed under associated data naming another owner, so it doesn't open as this one's.

vectors.name: agents_list_sealed_to_another_key
vectors.why: Only the owner's own sealing key opens it.

vectors.name: agents_list_opened_naming_another_owner
vectors.why: Signed by this owner but naming another, so the page takes it for nobody's.

vectors.name: agents_list_opened_at_another_host
vectors.why: A page reads the list its own host keeps.

vectors.name: agents_list_of_an_owner_with_no_recovery_code_yet
vectors.why: Until the owner sets their recovery code there's no backup to name, so the list names none.

vectors.name: agents_list_naming_a_backup_before_the_code_is_set
vectors.why: No backup satisfies a rule set later, so a list naming one isn't the owner's.

vectors.name: agents_list_naming_no_backup_once_there_is_one
vectors.why: Once the ID commits to a backup, the list names it.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy
vectors.why: A sign-in's copy opens with its lock, under associated data naming the owner and the sign-in, to the reading key the owner's ID names.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_of_another_key
vectors.why: A host knows the owner, the sign-in and the lock's point, so it can lock a key of its own as well: what opens counts only if it's the ID's reading key.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_for_another_owner
vectors.why: A copy names the owner whose ID it's for.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_for_a_sign_in_that_doesnt_count
vectors.why: And a sign-in that counts now.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_sealed_for_another_sign_in
vectors.why: Sealed naming another sign-in, so it doesn't open as this one's.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_locked_to_another_lock
vectors.why: Only the lock it names opens it.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_with_another_version
vectors.why: A copy is version 1.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_with_an_unknown_field
vectors.why: Unknown fields are refused.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_naming_a_sign_in_badly
vectors.why: key is a sign-in's name, a lowercase hex SHA-256.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_naming_an_owner_badly
vectors.why: owner is an ID as IDs are spelled.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_spelled_another_way
vectors.why: A copy has one spelling, compact JSON with its fields in order.

vectors.name: reading_key_copy_of_a_second_sign_in
vectors.why: Each sign-in that counts has its own copy, for the same reading key.

vectors.name: owner_view
vectors.why: The agent's key signs what its Signet leaves its owner, naming both, so a host carrying it can't write one.

vectors.name: owner_view_signed_by_another_key
vectors.why: Anyone can seal to the owner, whose sealing key is public, so only the agent's signature says the view is its own.

vectors.name: owner_view_of_another_agent
vectors.why: A view names the agent whose key signed it.

vectors.name: owner_view_for_another_owner
vectors.why: And the owner it's for, so one owner's can't be shown to another.

vectors.name: owner_view_dated_ahead
vectors.why: It can't be dated later than the agent's clock allows.

vectors.name: owner_view_that_isnt_an_object
vectors.why: The view is the object a Signet writes.

vectors.name: owner_view_in_another_field_order
vectors.why: One encoding, ahead of the view.

vectors.name: owner_view_of_another_version
vectors.why: Version 1.

vectors.name: owner_view_by_an_id_with_a_key_statement
vectors.why: Only an owner's ID may have more than one key, so one that added one is never an agent's.

vectors.name: owner_view_under_another_type
vectors.why: A view has its own type, so nothing else an agent signs stands for one.

vectors.name: owner_call
vectors.why: The agent's Signet opens a call's body with its own sealing key, bound to the call's method and path and to the agent, and checks what's inside as it would on its own socket. `call` is the call's whole body as sent, and `sealing` the key's private scalar in hex.

expect.body: {"rules":"the rules the owner signed, as compact JWS"}

vectors.name: owner_call_posted
vectors.why: A call that posts is bound to POST, as one that puts is to PUT.

expect.body: {"where_paid":"where the owner gets paid, as compact JWS"}

vectors.name: owner_call_put_opened_as_a_post
vectors.why: A body sealed for PUT doesn't open as a POST to the same path, so an opener has to bind the method it was given.

vectors.name: owner_mail
vectors.why: Owner mail is the owner-call seal for POST /v0/owner-mail/{agent}, over `{"kind","signed"}` followed by spaces up to a multiple of 1024 bytes, so a host that keeps it can't read it or tell its kind by its size. `mail` is the whole body an owner's device leaves at the host, and `sealing` the agent's sealing key's private scalar in hex. Its Signet opens it for that call and no other, and reads the JSON with the spaces after it.

expect.signed: the owner's yes, as compact JWS

vectors.name: owner_mail_sealed_as_a_call_to_signet
vectors.why: The same thing sealed for a call to Signet's own listener isn't owner mail, so nothing sent to one opens as the other.

vectors.name: owner_call_too_big
vectors.why: A call is at most 360 KiB as sent, which Signet reads no more than, though this one is sealed as it should be and would open.

vectors.name: owner_call_sealed_for_another_path
vectors.why: A body sealed for one call doesn't open as another, so what was sent as a delegation isn't taken as rules.

vectors.name: owner_call_sealed_for_another_method
vectors.why: Nor for the same path by another method.

vectors.name: owner_call_sealed_for_another_agent
vectors.why: Nor at another agent's Signet, though it was sealed to this one's key.

vectors.name: owner_call_sealed_to_another_key
vectors.why: Only this agent's sealing key opens it.

vectors.name: owner_call_with_another_field
vectors.why: The body is the sealed note and nothing beside it, so nothing travels unsealed.

vectors.name: owner_call_with_padding
vectors.why: A sealed note has one spelling.

vectors.name: owner_call_unsealed
vectors.why: What the owner signed, sent as it would be on Signet's own socket, isn't taken here, as anyone on the way would read it.

input.call: {"rules":"the rules the owner signed, as compact JWS"}

vectors.why: A sealed note is at least its key and tag.
